issue.title: E2: Exact-candidate release train and steward
issue.description: Every sase release is a sealed candidate built once at its tag: the wheel and sdist plus an exact `sase-core-rs==X.Y.Z` with its full file set and digests. It is qualified against the published core, exercised on Linux and macOS, published from the retained bytes with digest-checked resume, and confirmed from PyPI before it is un-drafted. One stateless steward decides release merges and the core cut, and every blocked release names a typed reason and its owner.

Evidence: src/manifest.ts extractReleaserConfig maps config draft -> draft and force-tag-creation -> forceTag (lines ~1406-1407); candidate releases carry both (lines ~1204-1205); createRelease passes {draft, prerelease, forceTag} through (lines ~1326-1335); src/github-api.ts createRelease (lines ~681-702) creates the tag ref at once via git.createRef (ignoring 422 if it exists) then repos.createRelease with draft:true. Next run finds the previous release via tag scan (latestReleaseVersion walks branch tags), and draft releases leave their tags in place. Conclusion: handover can set draft:true + force-tag-creation:true; no fallback needed.
